To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a mutant of Rhizobial fredii USDA 205 was obtained by passage through acridine plates, that this mutant was cured of a 197-megadaton Sym plasmid, and that the mutant retained its symbiotic efficiency, but had reduced nitrogenase activity and delayed nodulation relative to the parent strain.
curing of the Sym plasmid in R. fredici USDA 206C resulted in a loss of at least two nifi gene copies and a reduction in symbiotic effectiveness.
the loss of the Sym plasmid and the associated loss of plasmids containing nif gene copies resulted in reduced nodulation and reduced nitrogen fixation by Rhizobiumfredii USDA 206.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the Sym plasmid in nodulation and symbiotic effectiveness of R. fredii.
the relationship between the loss of a Sym plasmid and reduced symbiotic effectiveness in a Rhizobium strain.
the role of Sym plasmids in the symbiotic effectiveness and nodulation kinetics of R. fredii strains.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the symbiotic effectiveness was decreased in USDA 206 compared with USDA 206C because of the loss of plasmdborne nif gene and nodulation function copies.
loss of plasmiddetermined nodulation functions and loss of plasmiddened nif gene copies resulted in reduced symbiotic effectiveness.
the loss of plasmodborne nif gene sequences in strain USDA 206 C was responsible for the reduction in symbiotic effectiveness of this strain relative to strain USDA. 206.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
plasmid curing has a significant effect on symbiotic effectiveness of Rhizobial strain USDA 206, which is a strain of R. fredii.
the Sym plasmid is required for the expression of the full symbiotic potential of R. fredii strain USDA 206.
the Sym plasmid of strain USDA 606 is required for optimal symbiotic effectiveness in soybean.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Sym plasmid of R. fredii plays a significant role in the symbiotic effectiveness and nodulation efficiency of the strain.
the Sym plasmid of R. fredii strain USDA 206 is required for full symbiotic effectiveness.
the presence of Sym plasmids is not essential for symbiotic effectiveness of R. fredii.
